summary: Two commands had non-functional placeholder values in their `Example:` text (`--rows '[...]'`, `--cred-deb example-value`) fixed to real, runnable values; three commands whose positional legitimately has no invalid-input error case (a free-text search, a local-store lookup where "not found" is a valid empty result, a raw API passthrough the live API itself doesn't validate its path param for) are annotated `pp:no-error-path-probe`.
reason: Discovered running live Phase 5 acceptance with a real read-only token: `mutation create` and `mutation get-outstanding-invoices`'s `Example:` fields used copy-paste-looking but non-functional placeholders, which is a real (minor) doc bug independent of testing -- a user following the example verbatim would hit the same parse/validation error the live dogfood harness did. `mutation suggest <description>` and `relation statement <relation-id>` are novel (hand-authored) commands, so the generator's automatic `pp:no-error-path-probe` detection (`endpointSkipsErrorPathProbe`, spec-derived single free-text positional) never runs on them. `swagger get <catchAll>`'s single positional is a path param, so that same auto-detection correctly declines to exempt it in the general case (path-param positionals should usually be probed) -- this specific upstream endpoint just happens not to validate its path parameter, a legitimate hand-annotated exception matching the same pattern already used in the generator's own `tail.go.tmpl`.
call_sites: Annotations: map[string]string{... "pp:no-error-path-probe": "true"}  // mutation suggest, relation statement, swagger get
validated_outcome: Live Phase 5 dogfood run with a real read-only token: verdict PASS, 151/151, 0 failed (previously 7 failing test cases across these 5 commands). go build/vet/test all pass.
